# Libraries

```{r}
# load libraries
library(FLCore)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

library(ggforce) # for convex hull
library(mgcv)

library(metR)
library(concaveman)
library(ggpubr)

library(sf)
library(sfheaders)
# library(sp)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 16))
```

# Data preparation

Data preparation: 

```{r}
# load object from WGHANSA 2022
load(file.path("..","data","aneq.stk.RData")) # aneq.stk

# remove 2023

aneq.stk <- window(aneq.stk, end=2022)

# recruitment (1st January)
# change units

rec <- rec(aneq.stk)
rec <- rec*1e-6
units(rec) <- "1e9"

# ssb (from FLBiols because it is the same as used in FLBEIA)

aneq.biol <- as(aneq.stk, "FLBiol")
ssb <- ssb(aneq.biol)
# equivalently, (i.e. without fishing mortality)
# quantSums(stock.n(aneq.stk)*exp(-m(aneq.stk)*m.spwn(aneq.stk))*stock.wt(aneq.stk)*mat(aneq.stk))
ssb <- ssb/1000
units(ssb) <- "1000 t"

# create data frame

df <- data.frame(year=as.numeric(dimnames(aneq.stk)$year), 
                 rec=as.numeric(rec), 
                 ssb=as.numeric(ssb))

# create log variables

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(logr=log(rec),
         logssb=log(ssb),
         rat=rec/ssb, 
         lograt=log(rat))

dat <- read.csv(file.path("..","data","env_data.csv"), sep=",")

df <- left_join(df, dat)
df <- subset(df, select=-c(date)) # remove the date column (which is a character)
names(df)
range(df$year)
head(df)
tail(df)
```
Correlation between UI and TURB.q3: 

```{r}
cor(df$UI, df$TURB.q3, use="complete.obs")
cor.test(df$UI, df$TURB.q3, use="complete.obs")
cor(df$UI, df$TURB.q3, method="spearman", use="complete.obs")
cor.test(df$UI, df$TURB.q3, method="spearman", use="complete.obs")

summary(lm(TURB.q3~UI, data=df))
```

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(UI, TURB.q3))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", col=2, fill=2)+
  geom_smooth(col=3, fill=3)

ggplot(df, aes(UI, TURB.q3))+
  geom_point()+
  stat_ellipse(geom="polygon", col=1, 
                      alpha = 0.2,
                      show.legend = FALSE, 
                      level = 0.95)
```

# Basic Ricker + environmental covariates

## Models

```{r}

# given that there are no environmental data in 2022, the reference model is until 2021
mm10 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + UI + s(TURB.q3), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(mm10)

# Ricker without environmental variables
m0 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb, data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(m0)

# data
summary(df$UI)
summary(df$TURB.q3)
summary(df$ssb)
```

## Predictive plots: Turbulence 

```{r}

pred.dat <- expand.grid(UI=seq(100, 2000, by=300), TURB.q3=seq(100, 600, by=100), ssb=seq(10, 2500, by=10))
pred.dat$logssb <- log(pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$logr <- predict(mm10, newdata=pred.dat)
pred.dat$rec <- exp(pred.dat$logr)
pred.dat$rec.ref <- exp(predict(m0, newdata=pred.dat))

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(ssb, rec, group=TURB.q3, col=TURB.q3))+
  geom_line()+
  facet_wrap(~UI)+
  geom_line(data=pred.dat, aes(ssb, rec.ref), col=2)


pred.dat <- expand.grid(UI=mean(df$UI, na.rm=T), TURB.q3=seq(100, 600, by=100), ssb=seq(10, 2500, by=10))
pred.dat$logssb <- log(pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$logr <- predict(mm10, newdata=pred.dat)
pred.dat$rec <- exp(pred.dat$logr)
pred.dat$rec.ref <- exp(predict(m0, newdata=pred.dat))

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(ssb, rec, group=TURB.q3, col=TURB.q3))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(ssb, rec))+
  geom_line(data=pred.dat, aes(ssb, rec.ref), col=2)
```

# Joint effects

We fixed SSB at the value at which more or less the maximum is attained (SSB=500). And we look at combinations of turbulence and upwelling that lead to high Recruitment values.

```{r}
pred.dat <- expand.grid(UI=seq(100, 2000, by=300), TURB.q3=seq(100, 600, by=100), ssb=500)
pred.dat$logssb <- log(pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$logr <- predict(mm10, newdata=pred.dat)
pred.dat$rec <- exp(pred.dat$logr)
pred.dat$rec.ref <- exp(predict(m0, newdata=pred.dat))

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec, fill=rec))+
  geom_tile()+
  scale_fill_viridis_c()+
  geom_contour(col=2)+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec, fill=rec))+
  geom_contour(aes(colour = stat(level))) +
  metR::geom_text_contour(aes(z = rec), stroke = 0.15)+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2) 

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  metR::geom_text_contour(stroke = 0.15)+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)
```

```{r}
ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)+
  geom_mark_ellipse(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), expand=0, col=2)

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)+
  geom_mark_rect(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), expand=0, col=2)
```

## Option 1

Using the function chull (without margin)

```{r}
hull <- df %>% 
  select(UI, TURB.q3) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  slice(chull(UI, TURB.q3))
data.frame(hull)

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)+
  geom_polygon(data=hull, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2, fill=NA, inherit.aes = F)
```

## Option 3

Using stat_chull from ggpubr (without margin)

```{r}
p <- ggscatter(data=df, x="UI", y="TURB.q3")+
  stat_chull(alpha = 0.1, geom = "polygon")
print(p)

hull3 <- ggplot_build(p)$data[[2]] # extract data from ggplot

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)+
  geom_polygon(data=hull3, aes(x, y), col=2, fill=NA, inherit.aes = F)

```

## Option 4

Using package sf for spatial analysis

```{r}
points.sf <- st_as_sf(na.omit(subset(df, select=c("UI","TURB.q3"))), coords=c("UI","TURB.q3"))

hull4 <- st_convex_hull(st_union(points.sf)) # without buffer
hull5 <- st_buffer(hull4, dist=50) # with buffer

hull4 <- as.data.frame(st_coordinates(hull4)[,1:2]) # extract coordinates
hull5 <- as.data.frame(st_coordinates(hull5)[,1:2])
names(hull4) <- names(hull5) <- c("UI","TURB.q3")

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)+
  geom_polygon(data=hull4, aes(UI, TURB.q3), inherit.aes=F, col=2, fill=NA)+
  geom_polygon(data=hull5, aes(UI, TURB.q3), inherit.aes=F, col=3, fill=NA)

```

## Check if points are within the polygon limits using sf

```{r}
k <- 20
test <- data.frame(UI=runif(k, min(df$UI, na.rm=T), max(df$UI, na.rm=T)),
                   TURB.q3=runif(k, min(df$TURB.q3, na.rm=T), max(df$TURB.q3, na.rm=T)))

# using the package sp
# kk <- sp::point.in.polygon(test$UI, test$TURB.q3, hull$UI, hull$TURB.q3)

# using the package sf

test.sf <- st_as_sf(test, coords=c("UI","TURB.q3"))

hull.sf <- sfheaders::sf_polygon(obj = hull)
sel <- st_within(test.sf, hull.sf, sparse=F)
# alternatively 
# sel <- st_intersects(test.sf, hull4, sparse=FALSE)

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)+
  geom_polygon(data=hull, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2, fill=NA, inherit.aes = F)+
  geom_point(data=test, aes(UI, TURB.q3), pch=3, col="white", inherit.aes = F)+
  geom_point(data=test[sel,], aes(UI, TURB.q3), pch=3, col=2, inherit.aes = F)
  
hull5.sf <- sfheaders::sf_polygon(obj = hull5)
sel5 <- st_within(test.sf, hull5.sf, sparse=F)

ggplot(pred.dat, aes(UI, TURB.q3, z=rec))+
  metR::geom_contour_fill() +
  geom_contour(colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2)+
  geom_polygon(data=hull5, aes(UI, TURB.q3), col=2, fill=NA, inherit.aes = F)+
  geom_point(data=test, aes(UI, TURB.q3), pch=3, col="white", inherit.aes = F)+
  geom_point(data=test[sel5,], aes(UI, TURB.q3), pch=3, col=2, inherit.aes = F)

```
